samples.summary: The unterminated-directive strip test's only assertion holds even if the strip destroys the whole diagram
samples.evidence: `it('strips an unterminated config directive, which mermaid still reads')` (preview.test.ts:534-546) renders `%%{init: {"themeCSS": ...}` followed by `flowchart LR\n  A-->B` and asserts only `expect(source).not.toContain('themeCSS')`. `DIRECTIVE_RE` (mermaid.ts:209) has the closing `}%%` optional and its fourth alternative `((?:(?!}%{2}).|\r?\n)*)` matches greedily across newlines, so for this input the strip consumes the rest of the fence body and `mermaid.render` is called with (effectively) an empty diagram. The assertion passes regardless. Note the three sibling strip tests (lines 559, 574, 587) DO assert the diagram body survives (`toContain('flowchart LR')` / `startsWith('flowchart LR')`); this one omits exactly that assertion, so it provides no evidence that the documented 'stripped exactly as far as mermaid would have read it' behavior is right — it would pass under a strip that eats everything.

samples.summary: No test covers the unconditional cleanup of mermaid's `d<id>` layout host div
samples.evidence: mermaid.ts:477-485 adds a `finally` block that removes `document.getElementById('d'+id)`, justified in a long comment as preventing one leaked host (containing un-DOMPurified engine output) per keystroke on the failure path. No test creates such a host: grepping packages/notes/src for `getElementById` finds only the production line, and the stub engine (preview.test.ts:235-242) never appends anything to `document.body`, so this branch is entirely uncovered and could be deleted without any test failing. It is trivially testable — the stub receives `id` as its first argument.
searchedFor: read preview.test.ts mermaid describe block in full

samples.summary: The DOMPurify-load-failure degradation path has no test and no injection seam
samples.evidence: `loadPurifier()` (mermaid.ts:157-160) resolves `null` on a failed import and `renderPass` (mermaid.ts:431) then aborts, which the file documents as an intentional 'placeholders keep showing their source' degradation. Unlike the engine, the purifier has no injectable loader (`renderMermaidBlocks` options are only `theme`/`load`), so no test exercises it; the engine-failure analogue is tested at preview.test.ts:314-331 but says nothing about the purifier branch. Grep for `loadPurifier`/`purif` across packages/notes/src finds only the production definition and call site.
searchedFor: read full mermaid describe block in preview.test.ts

samples.summary: The extended `secure` key list passed to mermaid.initialize is never asserted
samples.evidence: `SECURE_KEYS` (mermaid.ts:167-184) is the security layer that pins theming keys (`themeCSS`, `themeVariables`, `htmlLabels`, ...) against nested directive overrides, and is described in the header comment as load-bearing. The only initialize assertions are `expect.objectContaining({ theme: 'dark' })` (preview.test.ts:724) and `expect.objectContaining({ theme: 'dark', securityLevel: 'strict' })` (preview.test.ts:756) — both pass if `secure` were dropped or emptied. Adding `secure: expect.arrayContaining([...])` would close it.
searchedFor: read all initialize assertions in preview.test.ts

`, so with no `}%%` in the body it greedily consumes to the end of the fence; stripConfigDirectives (mermaid.ts:226-228) feeds that result to mermaid.render (mermaid.ts:468), so the stub receives an effectively empty diagram and the lone assertion still passes. finding.summary: `img` assertion in the escaped-CSS test cannot fail — the element it looks for could never have existed
finding.evidence: In `drops CSS whose fetch is spelled with escapes, and img entirely` (preview.test.ts:421-446) the `` is placed INSIDE the second `

verdict.reason: The described code does not exist. The test at preview.test.ts:440-471 is named 'drops CSS whose fetch is spelled with escapes, and fetching tags' (not '...and img entirely'), contains no 'img src=x onerror=alert(1)' anywhere in the file, and has only ONE style element (lines 449-450), explicitly closed with a closing style tag before any img appears. The two img elements are separate sibling markup outside the style: line 452 (img src=https://evil.example/pixel.png) and line 453 inside foreignObject/div. The test's own comment (lines 443-445) states exactly the point the reviewer says it misses: 'The fetch-capable tags are separate markup, not text inside a style: an img there would be removed with the block that carries it, which would say nothing about FORBID_TAGS.' The assertion at line 465 is therefore falsifiable: it exercises FORBID_TAGS (mermaid.ts:249); foreignObject is registered as an HTML integration point (mermaid.ts:245) so the label-subtree img parses inside the svg subtree, sanitizeSvg returns the whole fragment (mermaid.ts:319-341) and apply() clones it wholesale (mermaid.ts:499) - removing 'img' from FORBID_TAGS would make querySelector('img') non-null and fail the assertion. The escaped-CSS style assertion (line 462) is separately backed by isSafeCss/decodeCssEscapes (mermaid.ts:284-301), and the serialize/re-parse element-child case has its own dedicated test at lines 473-495. The cited test makes no mutation-XSS/re-parse claim.
